title: Future Round: Alpha-R1 Dynamic Factor Gating on Strategy Library
rationale: Alpha-R1 (arXiv:2512.23515, Dec 2025, FinStep AI) is an 8B RL-trained reasoning model that dynamically activates or deactivates alpha factors based on current market regime and news context. Tested on CSI 300: Sharpe 1.62, 27.59% AR; zero-shot on CSI 1000: Sharpe 4.03, 78.18% AR. Massively outperforms static XGBoost (−21.65% AR). The core insight is that factor relevance is regime-conditional — momentum works in trending markets, mean-reversion in ranging markets — and an LLM trained via RL can learn WHEN each factor category is relevant. Applied to our 146-strategy library, this could function as a meta-layer that activates top-ranked strategies per regime and deactivates others. Trained on Chinese equities but architecture is market-agnostic; GitHub code available. This is a Round 33+ concept once R28–R32 are complete.
content:
### Alpha-R1: RL-Trained Dynamic Factor Gating (arXiv:2512.23515, Dec 2025)
- Architecture: 8B reasoning model trained via GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization — critic-free RL)
- Inputs: (1) semantic factor descriptions (economic rationale for each factor), (2) weekly market state summaries (price + news), (3) 82 Alpha101 candidate factors
- Mechanism: each day, model reasons over factor logic + market context → activates subset of factors → fixed linear scorer applies only those factors
- RL reward: backtested excess return × (1 − consistency_penalty) — penalizes incoherent factor selection
- Performance (2025 holdout): CSI 300 Sharpe 1.62 / 27.59% AR / 6.76% max DD; CSI 1000 zero-shot Sharpe 4.03 / 78.18% AR
- GitHub: https://github.com/FinStep-AI/Alpha-R1
- George application → Round 33 (concept): apply Alpha-R1-style gating to our 146-strategy library
  → Map each strategy to its factor category (momentum, mean-reversion, event-driven, macro)
  → Build weekly market state summaries from FRED data (macro) + VIX + SPY trend
  → RL-train gating model on past round results (treat each strategy as a 'factor')
  → NOTE: Original trained on CSI 300 (China). US adaptation needs US alpha factor library + retraining.
